name: Tokyo, Japan 🇯🇵
subtitle: More Michelin stars than any city on earth
items: Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (Ginza, Jiro Ono — the sushi that made a documentary)
Narisawa (Minami Aoyama, Yoshihiro Narisawa — innovative, World's 50 Best)
Den (Jimbocho, Zaiyu Hasegawa, 2-star — playful kaiseki, beloved worldwide)
Quintessence (Shirokanedai, Jacques Borie, 3-star French in Tokyo — yes)
Sushi Saito (reservation near-impossible unless you have a connection)
Tempura Kondo (Ginza, 2-star, the benchmark for tempura)
Kikunoi Honten (Akasaka, kaiseki royalty, 3-star)
L'Effervescence (Nishi Azabu, Shinobu Namae, 2-star)
Ichiran Ramen (solo dining booths — the original tonkotsu concept, multiple locations)
Afuri Ramen (Ebisu, yuzu salt — lighter, brighter than Ichiran)
Tsuta (Yoyogi-Uehara, first Michelin-starred ramen shop)
Gyukatsu Motomura (Shibuya, beef katsu — DIY on hot stone, always a queue)
Katsukura (Shinjuku, tonkatsu set meals — the refined version)
Kawaii Monster Café (Harajuku — an experience, not just a meal)
Ippudo Ramen (multiple — the other tonkotsu giant, a global original)
Shinjuku Golden Gai (alleyways of 6-seat bars — the whole area counts)
Ueno Ameyoko Market (street food, yakitori, fresh fish)
Tsukiji Outer Market (sushi breakfast at 7am — still the best after the inner market moved)
Fuglen Tokyo (Tomigaya, Norwegian coffee + cocktails)
Depachika food halls (basement of any Mitsukoshi or Isetan — the food universe)
